newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 10.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech-German Declaration, which was unexpectedly publicised yesterday, expresses the decisions of both sides to aim their relations towards the future. Czech Prime Minister, Vaclav Klaus, announced December 20 as the official date for initialising the document and stated that nothing important will be changed.
- The Czech Republic has decided to strengthen its preparations for negotiating EU membership, to clearly define its position and to form a quality team to carry out the negotiations.
- Yearly inflation will probably not exceed nine percent, nor is a drastic fall of inflation expected next year. The consumer price index grew by 0.5 percent in October month-on-month.

- As opposed to last year, when district administrations had a surplus of 4.8 billion crowns for first three quarters of the year, the situation this year has taken a worse turn with a deficit of 1.3 billion crowns recorded. Regional expenditures exceeded their revenues by 3.4 billion crowns over last year leading to a 4.6 billion crowns deficit.

- The employees of utility CEZ are threatening to strike if their employer does not agree to raise their wages by 25 percent next year. The chairman of the workers' union stated that although they do not want to disrupt the lives of citizens during the holidays, but the strike could mean a 10 to 15 minute reduction in power.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale (BLG), one of the four biggest banks in Germany, has recieved central bank permission to buy shares of Prague's Interbank. BLG will be able to buy 55 per cent of Interbank's shares directly while the Hungarian bank Magyar Kulkereskedelmi, majority-owned by BLG, will have the power to get the other 45 per cent of shares.
